name: Isaac Royall House

dates.altered: The survey's data form: 'Remodeled and enlarged 1733-37, 1747-50', over a core it dates 'Pre-1697'.
dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox prints 1732; the survey form dates the core 'Pre-1697' and the enlargements 1733-37 and 1747-50; the node's exemplar says built out in the 1730s and raised to three storeys in the 1740s. Recorded as the infobox states it, with the survey's two campaigns noted.

refs.title: Colonel Isaac Royall House, Main Street, between George & Royall Streets, Medford, Middlesex County, MA
refs.note: Call number HABS MASS,9-MED,1-. The survey number is read from the data page's own addendum header ('Addendum to Colonel Isaac Royall House HABS No. MA-577 (Usher-Royall House)') and the 1983 form ('HABS MA- NO. -577').

refs.title: Colonel Isaac Royall Slave Quarters, 15 George Street, Medford, Middlesex County, MA
refs.note: The SLAVE QUARTERS, a separate HABS record (the search hit prints 'Survey number: HABS MA-130'); carried because the node's own exemplar note says the surviving quarters are what make the house the most historically important Georgian house in New England.

quotes.text: DATE OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDE SOURCE) Pre-1697 ARCHITECT(S) (INCLUDE SOURCE) SIGNIFICANCE (ARCHITECTURAL AND HISTORICAL, INCLUDE ORIGINAL USE OF STRUCTURE) One of the few existing brick houses of the 17 th century. STYLE (IF APPROPRIATE} Federal MATERIAL OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDE STRUCTURAL SYSTEMS) Brick and fraqie with clapboarding
quotes.page: HABS No. MA-577, Architectural Data Form (Form 10-920, June 1983); no page number on the form. The form's STYLE field reads 'Federal' and its significance line calls the house a 17th-century brick house; both are quoted as printed.

quotes.text: EXTERIOR FEATURES OF NOTE Wooden imitation: tiasonry, gabled brick ends terminating in tall chimney stacks, wooden west front rusticated and adorned with a colossal order, quoining (among the earliest examples)
